research.summary:
Research done 2026-10-11. I checked npm, GitHub, jsDelivr and the m3.material.io pages (rendered in a browser). Labels: [F] = verified fact with its source URL. [I] = my inference or recommendation. [M] = a size I measured myself by gzip -9 of the jsDelivr file on 2026-10-11.

1) "Latest Material Design" means Material 3 plus the M3 Expressive update.
[F] Google announced M3 Expressive on May 13, 2025 and says it is not "M4" and does not deprecate M3. It adds 14 new or updated components: button groups, FAB menu, loading indicator, split button, toolbars, plus updated app bars, buttons, FABs, icon buttons, navigation bar and rail, progress indicators and sliders. It also adds a spring-based motion-physics system, emphasized typography, a library of 35 shapes with shape morphing, and more vibrant color schemes. https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive

2) Google's official web status.
[F] The official page for Material on the web says: "Material Web Components are currently in maintenance mode… Material 3 Expressive is not implemented on Web." It says Angular Material's "implementation may differ" from the guidelines. https://m3.material.io/develop/web
[F] The shape-morph page says "Web is not currently available." https://m3.material.io/styles/shape/shape-morph
[F] The motion page lists web as "Compatible with Compose springs" and publishes a table converting springs to cubic-bezier curves. https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview/specs

3) What is new in 2026.
[F] Even though @material/web (MWC) is still labelled maintenance mode, Google shipped v2.5.0 on 2026-07-14. It adds experimental "Labs" components: expressive button, FAB, icon, list, menu and split button, plus CSS utility classes, a Tailwind theme, and expressive token files. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/releases/tag/v2.5.0
[F] Labs work continued after that release. Commits added a toolbar (Sep 21), tabs (Sep 24), button group, navigation bar and slider (Sep 29), and snackbar (Oct 7, 2026). A nightly build, 2.5.1-nightly.47adb65.0, was published 2026-10-08. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/commits/main and https://www.npmjs.com/package/@material/web?activeTab=versions
[F] The Labs README says the folder is "not recommended for production." https://github.com/material-components/material-web/tree/main/labs
[I] Google appears to be quietly rebuilding Expressive for the web inside MWC Labs, but nothing is production-ready or officially announced.

4) Third-party libraries.
[F] The only actively maintained web-component library with broad M3 Expressive coverage today is M3E (@m3e/web 2.10.0, published 2026-10-11, Lit, MIT). It has one main maintainer, with 1,441 commits; no other contributor has more than 8. https://github.com/matraic/m3e and https://api.github.com/repos/matraic/m3e/contributors
[F] mdui v2 is a stable M3 baseline library (not Expressive). Its README says v3 will be based on M3 Expressive, but the v3 branch was last updated 2025-08-13. https://github.com/zdhxiong/mdui
[F] Beer CSS 5.0.3 is a CSS framework that claims "Latest M3 Expressive already." https://github.com/beercss/beercss
[F] MUI still targets Material Design 2. https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/master/docs/data/material/getting-started/overview/overview.md

5) Building the theme ourselves.
[F] The official building blocks are public: @material/material-color-utilities 0.4.0 supports SpecVersion '2025' and an EXPRESSIVE variant, and @material/web 2.5.0 ships autogenerated token files from design system v34.0.21 that include spring stiffness and damping values.
[I] So we can get the M3 Expressive look in either Lit or Preact even though no library ships it completely or officially.

options.name: Material Web Components (MWC), stable component set
options.latest_version: 2.5.0 [F] (dist-tag latest). There is also a nightly, 2.5.1-nightly.47adb65.0, from 2026-10-08 [F]. https://registry.npmjs.org/@material/web
options.last_release_date: 2026-07-14 per the changelog; npm publish was 2026-07-15 [F]. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/releases/tag/v2.5.0
options.maintenance_status:
[F] Maintenance mode was announced 2024-06-10 in GitHub discussion #5642. The post says MWC is not deprecated, but Material Design is "no longer actively staffing its development" and new features are not planned. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/discussions/5642
[F] In May 2025 a maintainer replied there: "new Expressive features are not planned for MWC." (same URL)
[F] The README still reads "MWC is in maintenance mode pending new maintainers." The roadmap was reviewed 2026-07-31 and says no work is planned. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
[F] In practice Google engineers still commit through copybara: security fixes (safevalues href sanitization, Sep 2026), TypeScript 6 fixes, and a lot of Labs work. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/commits/main
[F] It has 11.3k GitHub stars.
options.m3_coverage:
[F] M3 baseline only, no Expressive in the stable set. https://m3.material.io/develop/web
[F] Stable components: buttons, icon buttons, FAB, checkbox, radio, switch, chips, dialog, divider, elevation, focus ring, icon, list, menu, progress (linear and circular), ripple, select, slider, tabs, text field.
[F] The roadmap lists these as never built: autocomplete, badge, banner, bottom app bar, bottom sheet, card, data table, date picker, navigation bar, navigation drawer, navigation rail, search, segmented button, snackbar, time picker, top app bar, tooltip. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
[F] Its theming docs say MWC does not support --md-ref-palette or --md-sys-motion tokens. https://material-web.dev/theming/material-theming/
options.framework_fit:
[F] It is built with Lit and uses Shadow DOM. https://github.com/material-components/material-web
[I] It fits a Lit app natively. It also works in Preact as custom elements, but then Lit ships alongside Preact.
options.bundle_size:
[F] all.js is 72.1 KB gzip and common.js is 53.7 KB gzip; a single button is about 7 KB gzip. These are the project's own figures, updated 2025-08-20. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/docs/size.md
[M] all.js via jsDelivr +esm: 71.9 KB gzip.
options.theming: [F] Theming uses CSS custom properties: --md-sys-color-*, --md-ref-typeface-brand and --md-ref-typeface-plain, --md-sys-typescale-*, --md-sys-shape-corner-*, and per-component tokens such as --md-filled-button-container-shape. Tokens can be scoped with CSS selectors. https://material-web.dev/theming/material-theming/
options.pros:
[F] Google-authored, accessible, form-associated controls, Shadow-DOM encapsulated, Apache-2.0. Security fixes still land in 2026.
[I] Its form controls (text field, select, checkbox, switch, slider, dialog, menu, chips) are the most battle-tested M3 controls on the web, which suits the admin SPA.
options.cons:
[F] Officially in maintenance mode, and M3 Expressive is officially "not implemented on Web."
[F] It has no navigation rail, navigation bar, bottom sheet, side sheet, snackbar, data table or date picker, which a map viewer and an admin need. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
[I] It looks like 2023-era M3, not the latest look the user asked for.

options.name: MWC Labs 'gb': Google's experimental M3 Expressive work
options.latest_version:
[F] 2.5.0 contains CSS and elements for badge, button, card, checkbox, divider, FAB, focus ring, icon button, list, menu, radio, ripple, split button, switch and the tokens. https://unpkg.com/@material/web@2.5.0/labs/gb/?meta
[F] main and nightly add toolbar, tabs, button group, navigation bar, slider and snackbar. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/tree/main/labs/gb
options.maintenance_status:
[F] Under active development by Google engineers, with commits from Jul to Oct 2026. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/commits/main
[F] The Labs README says the code is "not recommended for production" and that breaking changes can happen without a major version bump. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/tree/main/labs
[F] The token-files README says they "may introduce breaking changes at any point across minor and patch updates" and advises pinning the exact version. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/README.md
options.m3_coverage:
[F] Expressive features are present: button sizes xs to xl, square and round toggle shapes, split button, FAB, button group, toolbar, navigation bar, and the new shape tokens (corner-lg-increased 20px, xl-increased 32px, xxl 48px).
[F] The token set includes M3 Expressive component tokens: button-group, split-button, toolbar-floating and toolbar-docked, loading-indicator, nav-rail-collapsed and nav-rail-expanded, fab-menu, app-bar flexible, sheet-side and sheet-bottom. It also includes md.sys.motion.spring.* stiffness and damping values from design system version 34.0.21. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/latest/sass/_md-sys-motion.scss
[F] Its typography tokens include emphasized styles that set the 'ROND' 100 font axis. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material/web@2.5.0/labs/gb/styles/typography/md-typography-tokens.css
options.framework_fit:
[F] CSS-first: utility classes such as .btn.btn-filled.btn-md live in @layer md.comp.*. There are optional Lit elements (md-gb-button and others) and an adoptStyles() helper that can attach the sheets to a document or a shadow root. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/labs/gb/styles/adopt-styles.ts
[I] Because it is CSS-first, the class CSS can also be used from Preact markup inside a shadow root. The system-token sheets target :root, so they would need rewriting to :host to work inside Shadow DOM.
options.bundle_size: [M] The full token sheet labs/gb/styles/m3.css is 2.2 KB gzip (13.5 KB raw). The button CSS is 5.9 KB raw.
options.theming: [F] It uses the same --md-sys-color-* names with light-dark() values and color-scheme: light dark, plus --md-sys-shape-corner-{xs,sm,md,lg,lg-increased,xl,xl-increased,xxl,full}, --md-sys-typescale-* shorthand (for example label-lg), and --md-sys-motion-easing-* and duration-*. There is also a Tailwind v4 @theme mapping (labs/gb/styles/tailwind.css). https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material/web@2.5.0/labs/gb/styles/color/md-color-tokens.css
options.pros:
[F] It is Google's own code and token source, Apache-2.0, small, modern CSS (@layer, light-dark(), container-relative units).
[I] It is the best place to copy authoritative Expressive token values from, and the most likely future official web implementation.
options.cons:
[F] Labeled not for production, may break in minor releases, and undocumented on the public site. The official M3 web page still says Expressive is not implemented on the web.
[I] The API could change or be dropped. Vendor the CSS you need and pin the exact version rather than depending on it at runtime.

options.name: M3E (Material 3 Expressive web components)
options.last_release_date: [F] npm publish 2026-10-11; the repo was pushed 2026-10-11. https://github.com/matraic/m3e
options.maintenance_status:
[F] Very active. The repo was created 2025-09-21 and has 299 stars, MIT license.
[F] One maintainer (matraic) has 1,441 commits; no other contributor has more than 8. https://api.github.com/repos/matraic/m3e/contributors
[F] The repo says it is not affiliated with Google. https://github.com/matraic/m3e
[I] The main risk is the bus factor: one person maintains it.
options.m3_coverage:
[F] Broadest Expressive coverage on the web, about 60 components: app bar, autocomplete, avatar, badge, bottom sheet, breadcrumb, button, button group, calendar, card, checkbox, chips, content pane, date input, datepicker, dialog, divider, drawer container, expansion panel, FAB, FAB menu, form field, gestures, icon, icon button, list, loading indicator, menu, nav bar, nav menu, nav rail, paginator, progress indicator, radio group, search, segmented button, select, shape, skeleton, slide group, slider, snackbar, split button, split pane, stepper, switch, tabs, theme, timepicker, toolbar, tooltip, tree. https://matraic.github.io/m3e/ and https://www.npmjs.com/package/@m3e/web
[F] m3e-shape includes all 35 Material shapes and morphing. https://github.com/matraic/m3e/blob/main/packages/web/src/shape/README.md
[F] From reading the bundle: it morphs with clip-path: polygon() transitions and implements springs as CSS variables (--md-sys-motion-spring-*) holding the official web cubic-bezier conversions. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@m3e/web@2.10.0/dist/core.min.js
[F] There is no data table component.
options.framework_fit:
[F] Built on Lit 3: the package declares lit ^3.3.0 as a peer dependency and depends on @floating-ui/dom and @material/material-color-utilities ^0.4.0. It uses Shadow DOM and adoptedStyleSheets. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@m3e/web@2.10.0/package.json
[I] Native fit for Lit; usable from Preact as custom elements.
options.bundle_size: [M] all.min.js 272 KB gzip, so import per component. core.min.js 23.6 KB, theme.min.js 26.7 KB, button 7.8 KB, slider 7.3 KB, bottom-sheet 5.8 KB, nav-rail 2.0 KB (all gzip).
options.theming: [F] An <m3e-theme> element takes color (seed hex), variant (tonal-spot, vibrant, expressive, fidelity, content, monochrome, neutral, rainbow, fruit-salad), scheme (auto, light, dark), contrast (standard, medium, high), density (0, -1, -2), motion (standard or expressive) and strong-focus. It writes --md-sys-color-* tokens. It changes <body> and documentElement only when it is a direct child of <body>; otherwise it scopes itself to :host. https://github.com/matraic/m3e/blob/main/packages/web/src/theme/README.md
options.pros:
[F] It has the Expressive components we need: nav rail (collapsed and expanded), flexible nav bar, toolbar, FAB menu, split button, button group, loading indicator, bottom sheet, datepicker and stepper. Dynamic color uses the official MCU 0.4.0. Shadow DOM isolates styles. MIT.
[I] Fastest route to a true Expressive look for both the viewer and the admin SPA.
options.cons:
[F] Single maintainer, young project, about 300 stars, not Google. The all-in-one bundle is heavy. No data table.
[I] The theme element alone (about 27 KB gzip, mostly color math) is a lot for an embed. Precompute colors at build time instead. Pin versions because the API may move fast.

options.name: mdui v2
options.last_release_date: [F] 2026-07-14 (npm); last commit to the v2 branch 2026-07-21. https://github.com/zdhxiong/mdui
options.maintenance_status:
[F] v2 is maintained with bug fixes; 4.5k stars, MIT.
[F] The README says: "I am developing mdui v3 based on the M3 Expressive specification." However, the v3 branch was last committed 2025-08-13. https://github.com/zdhxiong/mdui/commits/v3
[I] v3 appears stalled.
options.m3_coverage:
[F] M3 (Material You) baseline, not Expressive. 34 component folders: avatar, badge, bottom-app-bar, button, button-icon, card, checkbox, chip, circular-progress, collapse, dialog, divider, dropdown, FAB, icon, layout, linear-progress, list, menu, navigation-bar, navigation-drawer, navigation-rail, radio, range-slider, ripple, segmented-button, select, slider, snackbar, switch, tabs, text-field, tooltip, top-app-bar. It also has .mdui-table and .mdui-prose CSS classes. https://www.mdui.org/en/docs/2/llms.txt
[F] No date picker, no data-table component, no bottom or side sheet.
options.framework_fit:
[F] Web components built with Lit (dependencies include lit ^3.3.0) using Shadow DOM with ::part styling hooks. https://www.mdui.org/en/docs/2/getting-started/usage.md
[I] Natural fit for Lit; usable from Preact.
options.bundle_size: [M] mdui.esm.js (full) 83.5 KB gzip; mdui.css 3.5 KB gzip. [F] Imports can be per component. https://www.mdui.org/en/docs/2/getting-started/installation.md
options.theming:
[F] Uses its own tokens, --mdui-color-* as RGB triplets used like rgb(var(--mdui-color-primary)), plus --mdui-typescale-* and --mdui-shape-corner-*. setColorScheme() and getColorFromImage() build dynamic color; it depends on MCU ^0.3.0. https://www.mdui.org/en/docs/2/styles/design-tokens.md
[M] mdui.css declares tokens on :root and .mdui-theme-*.
options.pros: [F] Mature and stable, the most popular non-Google M3 web-component library, with navigation bar, rail and drawer, a responsive layout component, i18n and IDE tooling.
options.cons:
[F] Not Expressive; the Expressive v3 appears inactive; its token names do not match --md-sys-*.
[I] Its global :root tokens would need scoping for an embed. Using it would not satisfy "latest Material Design."

options.name: Beer CSS
options.m3_coverage: [F] The README claims "Latest M3 Expressive already." Elements: badge, button, card, checkbox, chip, dialog, divider, expansion, grid, icon, input, layout, list, main layout, media, menu, navigation (rail and bar), overlay, page, progress, radio, select, shape (35 shapes with built-in morphing), slider, snackbar, switch, table, tabs, textarea, tooltip, typography. https://github.com/beercss/beercss/blob/main/docs/ELEMENTS.md and https://github.com/beercss/beercss/blob/main/docs/SHAPE.md
options.framework_fit:
[F] A class-based CSS framework that works with any framework, including Preact or Lit. It offers a scoped build (styles under .beer) and a <beer-css> custom element that loads the scoped build. https://github.com/beercss/beercss
[M] The custom element does not use attachShadow.
options.bundle_size: [M] beer.min.css 16.9 KB gzip (the README badge says 14.5 KB brotli), beer.min.js 5.9 KB gzip, material-dynamic-colors 16.3 KB gzip. [F] 5.0.3 added a module build that can cut size by up to 10x. https://github.com/beercss/beercss/releases
options.theming:
[F] Light and dark via body classes; dynamic color through material-dynamic-colors.
[M] The default build styles html, body, *, a, span, article and other bare elements, so it leaks into a host page unless you use the scoped build.
options.pros: [F] Smallest way to get an Expressive-looking UI, with shapes and morphing, and a table element useful for admin data grids. No build step required.
options.cons: [I] It is CSS conventions, not accessible behavior components: you write ARIA and focus management yourself. It is not Shadow-DOM isolated, it is a single-maintainer-style project, and its "M3 Expressive" claim is self-reported. Its look is approximate rather than token-exact.

options.name: material-esm/material (community fork of MWC)
options.package: github:material-esm/material (installed from GitHub or via jsDelivr gh/, not npm)
options.maintenance_status: [F] Active (several releases in October 2026), 193 stars, Apache-2.0. The README asks users to sponsor before filing issues. https://github.com/material-esm/material
options.m3_coverage: [F] Adds components MWC lacks: app bar, badge, bottom sheet, card, carousel, navigation (rail and drawer), pickers, search, snackbar, tooltip. It links a "Material 3 Expressive demo." How complete its Expressive coverage is was not documented. https://github.com/material-esm/material
options.framework_fit: [F] Lit-based fork of MWC. [I] Fits Lit.
options.pros: [I] Familiar MWC API with the missing components filled in.
options.cons: [I] Small, sponsor-gated, not on npm, and of unclear long-term viability.

options.name: Angular Material (reference only)
options.maintenance_status: [F] Actively maintained by the Angular team. https://github.com/angular/components/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
options.m3_coverage:
[F] M3 theming with --mat-sys-* system tokens and M3 prebuilt themes. https://github.com/angular/components/blob/main/guides/theming.md
[F] I found no M3 Expressive entries in the changelog.
[F] A third-party layer, mat-expressive (@ngm-dev/mat-exp), adds Expressive on top. https://peerlist.io/shhdharmen/project/mat-expressive
[F] Google notes Angular Material's implementation "may differ" from the guidelines. https://m3.material.io/develop/web
options.framework_fit: Angular only, so not usable with Preact or Lit.
options.pros: [F] Google-backed and the only officially recommended Material path for Angular. https://github.com/material-components/material-web

options.name: MUI Material UI (reference only)
options.maintenance_status: [F] Very active, but v9 (April 2026) focused on accessibility, performance and Base UI, with no mention of Material Design 3. https://mui.com/blog/introducing-material-ui-v9/
options.m3_coverage:
[F] Its docs say "Material UI supports Material Design 2." https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/master/docs/data/material/getting-started/overview/overview.md
[F] The M3 tracking issue is still open; it was removed from the v8 milestone in Jan 2026, and a contributor said in May 2026 not to expect M3 this year. https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/29345
options.framework_fit: React; Preact only through preact/compat. Emotion CSS-in-JS injects into document.head.
options.pros: Huge ecosystem and data grid (MUI X).
options.cons: [F] Not M3. [I] It disqualifies itself for a "latest Material Design" requirement and for a small, non-leaking embed.

options.name: Vuetify (reference only)
options.maintenance_status: [F] Active. v4.0.0 shipped 2026-02-23 with MD3 typography and MD3 elevation levels. https://github.com/vuetifyjs/vuetify/releases/tag/v4.0.0
options.m3_coverage: [F] An MD3 'blueprint' preset exists, and its docs still say "Material Design 3 is currently in active development." No Expressive. https://github.com/vuetifyjs/vuetify/blob/master/packages/docs/src/pages/en/features/blueprints.md
options.pros: Rich admin components (data table, date picker).
options.cons: Vue only; partial MD3; no Expressive.

options.name: m3-svelte (reference only)
options.m3_coverage: [F] The demo site shows connected buttons (button groups), split buttons, a loading indicator, bottom sheet, nav rail, adaptive 'Nav for C/M/L/X', and a date field. Its peer dependency is a nightly build of material-color-utilities. https://kendell.dev/m3-svelte/ and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/m3-svelte@7.2.1/package.json
options.pros: [I] A good reference implementation of Expressive pieces to study.

options.name: Other small Lit-based M3 libraries
options.latest_version: [F] sober 1.1.10 (2026-03-28); @sandlada/mdc 0.2.0-20261008.a (nightly); material-web-additions repo last pushed 2025-10-17. https://github.com/apprat/sober, https://github.com/sandlada/mdc, https://github.com/maicol07/material-web-additions
options.maintenance_status: [F] sober has 242 stars and was pushed 2026-09-25. @sandlada/mdc has 3 stars and was forked from @material/web. material-web-additions has 32 stars and is dormant.
options.cons: [I] Too small or immature to depend on.

research.m3_expressive_status:
What M3 Expressive is
[F] Google announced it on 2025-05-13 as "an evolution of the Material 3 design system," backed by 46 studies with more than 18,000 participants. Google says it is not M4 and does not deprecate M3. https://m3.material.io/blog/building-with-m3-expressive
[F] Contents:
- 14 new or updated components: app bars, button groups (new), common buttons, extended FAB, FAB menu (new), FABs, icon buttons, loading indicator (new), navigation bar, navigation rail, progress indicators, sliders, split button (new), toolbars (new).
- A motion-physics system based on springs.
- Emphasized typography.
- A library of 35 shapes with shape morphing.
- More vibrant color schemes.
- Seven "expressive tactics," including limiting yourself to one or two "hero moments."
(same URL)

Official web status in 2026
[F] https://m3.material.io/develop/web says: "Material Web Components are currently in maintenance mode. No updates are currently being made to this library. Material 3 Expressive is not implemented on Web."
[F] Shape morph on the web: "Web is not currently available." https://m3.material.io/styles/shape/shape-morph
[F] Motion on the web is "Compatible": "Use springs when possible, otherwise use curves that mimic the springs." https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview/specs
[F] The navigation drawer is "no longer recommended"; use the expanded navigation rail instead, and the drawer is listed as "Unavailable" on the web. https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-drawer/overview
[F] The baseline navigation rail is "no longer recommended"; use the collapsed rail. https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-rail/specs
[F] Despite the official wording, Google is building Expressive web components in @material/web/labs (expressive buttons, FAB, menu, split button and lists shipped in 2.5.0; toolbar, tabs, button group, nav bar, slider and snackbar on main between Sep and Oct 2026). Labs is "not recommended for production." https://github.com/material-components/material-web/releases/tag/v2.5.0 and https://github.com/material-components/material-web/commits/main

Official tokens and specs available today for the web
1. Spring tokens [F], from @material/web 2.5.0, file tokens/versions/latest/sass/_md-sys-motion.scss, design system version 34.0.21. Stiffness / damping:
   - fast.spatial 1400 / 0.9
   - default.spatial 700 / 0.9
   - slow.spatial 300 / 0.9
   - fast.effects 3800 / 1
   - default.effects 1600 / 1
   - slow.effects 800 / 1
   The legacy easing tokens are there too, for example standard = cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) and emphasized-decelerate = cubic-bezier(0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1). https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/latest/sass/_md-sys-motion.scss
2. Official spring-to-curve conversions for the web [F] (https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview/specs):
   - Expressive fast spatial: cubic-bezier(0.42, 1.67, 0.21, 0.90), 350ms
   - Expressive default spatial: (0.38, 1.21, 0.22, 1.00), 500ms
   - Expressive slow spatial: (0.39, 1.29, 0.35, 0.98), 650ms
   - Expressive fast, default and slow effects: (0.31, 0.94, 0.34, 1) 150ms; (0.34, 0.80, 0.34, 1) 200ms; (0.34, 0.88, 0.34, 1) 300ms
   - Standard spatial: (0.27, 1.06, 0.18, 1) at 350, 500 and 750ms
   [F] Spatial springs (position, size, rotation, corner radius) overshoot; effects springs (color, opacity) do not. Use default speed for sheets and the expanded rail, fast for small components, slow for full-screen. https://m3.material.io/styles/motion/overview/how-it-works
3. Shape scale [F]: none 0, xs 4, sm 8, md 12, lg 16, lg-increased 20, xl 28, xl-increased 32, xxl 48, full. The increased sizes and xxl are new with Expressive. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/latest/sass/_md-sys-shape.scss
4. Emphasized typescale tokens [F] (_md-sys-typescale-emphasized.scss), including variable-font axes: wght, wdth, opsz, GRAD, ROND, slnt. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/tree/main/tokens/versions/latest/sass
5. Component tokens for the Expressive components [F]:
   - nav-rail-collapsed: width 96px (narrow 80px)
   - nav-rail-expanded: width 220 to 360px; modal version has radius corner-large
   - nav-bar: height 64px
   - toolbar-floating: 64px, corner-full, elevation level 3
   - sheet-side docked: 256px wide
   - sheet-bottom: corner-extra-large-top, drag handle 32 by 4px
   - loading-indicator, button-group, split-button, fab-menu, app-bar flexible
   https://github.com/material-components/material-web/tree/main/tokens/versions/latest/sass
6. Color [F]: @material/material-color-utilities 0.4.0 (2026-01-21) has SpecVersion '2021' | '2025' and variants MONOCHROME, NEUTRAL, TONAL_SPOT, VIBRANT, EXPRESSIVE, FIDELITY, CONTENT, RAINBOW, FRUIT_SALAD, with contrastLevel from -1 to 1. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material/material-color-utilities@0.4.0/dynamiccolor/color_spec.d.ts

Getting the M3 Expressive look on the web without a complete library [I]
- Color: generate light, dark, medium-contrast and high-contrast schemes at build time with MCU 0.4.0 (SchemeTonalSpot, or SchemeVibrant / SchemeExpressive for a bolder look, with specVersion '2025'). Emit --md-sys-color-* values, using light-dark() like Google's Labs CSS does. Use primary, secondary and tertiary containers to make hero actions stand out.
- Shape: use the full corner scale, mixing pill (full) buttons and FABs with 28 to 48px sheets and cards. Toggle buttons change from round to a square-ish radius when selected (Labs button CSS sets --container-shape to corner-md when selected). Use the 35 decorative shapes for photo-thumbnail crops and avatars. For morphing, either animate clip-path: polygon() between polygons with equal vertex counts (M3E's technique) or animate SVG paths. CSS shape() is "newly available" Baseline since 2026-02-24 (https://webstatus.dev/features/shape-function) and can be a progressive enhancement.
- Motion: put the official cubic-bezier conversions above into --md-sys-motion-spring-* custom properties. For real damped springs, generate CSS linear() easing from the official stiffness and damping. linear() is Baseline widely available since 2023-12 (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/easing-function/linear; generator: https://linear-easing-generator.netlify.app/). Use a JS spring engine only for interruptible gestures such as dragging a bottom sheet. Always provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback with no overshoot.
- Typography: use emphasized styles (heavier weight; ROND axis where the font supports it) for headlines, the active year in the timeline, and primary actions.
- Components to build or source: loading indicator, floating toolbar for the timeline, FAB menu (layers, compare, about), button group or connected segmented control (layer modes), split button, collapsed and expanded rail, flexible nav bar.
research.theming_details:
Color utilities
[F] @material/material-color-utilities latest is 0.4.0 (npm 2026-01-21, Apache-2.0). It exports DynamicScheme, MaterialDynamicColors, Hct, Scheme* classes (TonalSpot, Vibrant, Expressive, Fidelity, Content, Neutral, Monochrome, Rainbow, FruitSalad), the quantizers and Score (for extracting a seed color from an image), and the older themeFromSourceColor / applyTheme helpers. https://www.npmjs.com/package/@material/material-color-utilities and https://github.com/material-foundation/material-color-utilities/tree/main/typescript
[F] Scheme constructors take (sourceColorHct, isDark, contrastLevel, specVersion?, platform?). specVersion is '2021' or '2025'; platform is 'phone' or 'watch'. contrastLevel runs from -1 to 1; 0 is standard (medium and high are conventionally 0.5 and 1.0). https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material/material-color-utilities@0.4.0/scheme/scheme_tonal_spot.d.ts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material/material-color-utilities@0.4.0/dynamiccolor/dynamic_scheme.d.ts
[I] Run MCU in a Vite build script, not at runtime, and emit a static CSS token file. themeFromSourceColor / applyTheme are the older API; for the 2025 spec use MaterialDynamicColors with a DynamicScheme.
[F] GUI alternative: Material Theme Builder (https://material-foundation.github.io/material-theme-builder/, live at HTTP 200).

Token names (CSS custom properties)
[F] MWC and Labs use --md-sys-color-{primary, on-primary, primary-container, on-primary-container, primary-fixed, primary-fixed-dim, on-primary-fixed, on-primary-fixed-variant, the same set for secondary and tertiary, error, error-container, surface, surface-dim, surface-bright, surface-container-{lowest, low, (plain), high, highest}, on-surface, on-surface-variant, inverse-surface, inverse-on-surface, inverse-primary, outline, outline-variant, scrim, shadow, background}. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material/web@2.5.0/labs/gb/styles/color/md-color-tokens.css
[F] Typography:
- MWC: --md-ref-typeface-brand and --md-ref-typeface-plain, plus --md-sys-typescale-{display|headline|title|body|label}-{large|medium|small}-{font|size|line-height|weight|tracking}. https://material-web.dev/theming/material-theming/
- Labs: shorthand forms such as --md-sys-typescale-label-lg, --md-sys-typescale-emphasized-label-lg and *-axes.
[F] Other system tokens: --md-sys-shape-corner-*, --md-sys-motion-easing-* and duration-*, --md-sys-elevation-*, --md-sys-space-*.
[F] Library-specific names: Angular uses --mat-sys-*; mdui uses --mdui-color-* as RGB triplets; M3E uses --md-sys-* plus component-level --m3e-* variables.
[I] Standardize on --md-sys-*. MWC, MWC Labs and M3E all read those names, so one generated theme drives all three.

Embedding pitfalls with Shadow DOM [I, based on standard CSS behavior]
- Custom properties and inherited properties (font-family, color, line-height) flow from the host page into the shadow tree. Declare the full token set and the base font on :host so a host page that also uses --md-sys-* tokens cannot restyle the widget.
- A stylesheet adopted into a shadow root cannot match :root, so rewrite :root-scoped token sheets (such as the Labs m3.css) to :host.
- light-dark() needs color-scheme: light dark. It is Baseline "newly available" since 2024-05 (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/color_value/light-dark). Give older browsers a prefers-color-scheme fallback.

Fonts
[F] M3's fonts page says static Roboto is the default in M3 components. Roboto Flex is a variable font (axes: slnt, wdth, wght, GRAD, opsz, plus parametric axes) that is "not yet part of the M3 typescale." Recommended fallback order: Roboto Flex, then Roboto, then Noto Sans. https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/fonts
[F] The Labs typography tokens use "Roboto Flex, Roboto, Noto Sans, system-ui" and set 'ROND' 100 for emphasized styles. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@material/web@2.5.0/labs/gb/styles/typography/md-typography-tokens.css
[F] Google Sans Flex was released free and open source (SIL OFL) on Google Fonts in November 2025, with a ROND (roundness) axis, 0 to 100. https://designcompass.org/en/2025/11/19/google-sans-flex-font-released-for-free/ and https://fontsource.org/fonts/google-sans-flex
[F] The Google Fonts CSS2 API serves "Google Sans Flex" with wght 1–1000, wdth 25–151%, slnt, opsz, GRAD and ROND (verified 2026-10-11): https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Google+Sans+Flex:opsz,slnt,wdth,wght,GRAD,ROND@6..144,-10..0,25..151,1..1000,0..100,0..100
[F] It is also on npm as @fontsource-variable/google-sans-flex 5.3.2 (2026-10-11); Roboto Flex is @fontsource-variable/roboto-flex 5.3.0.
[I] For the Expressive look: Google Sans Flex (or Roboto Flex) first, then Roboto, Noto Sans and system-ui.
[F] Inside Shadow DOM, @font-face rules have historically been ignored, so fonts must be declared at document level. https://robdodson.me/posts/at-font-face-doesnt-work-in-shadow-dom/ and https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1077396
[I] The embed loader should inject one document-level stylesheet that only declares @font-face (namespaced family names, no selectors) and treat that as the single accepted global side effect. Alternatively, fall back to system-ui.

Icons
[F] Material Symbols is a variable icon font (Outlined, Rounded, Sharp; axes FILL 0–1, wght 100–700, GRAD -50–200, opsz 20–48) served by the Google Fonts CSS2 API. https://fonts.google.com/icons
[F] Per-icon SVG packages: @material-symbols/svg-400 0.48.0 (2026-10-09). https://www.npmjs.com/package/@material-symbols/svg-400
[I] For the embed, import only the inline SVG icons you use. This is tree-shakable, avoids the font-in-shadow-DOM problem, and avoids downloading a large icon font. Use Material Symbols Rounded with FILL 1 for selected states, which matches Expressive's fill-on-select behavior; the Labs commit "apply icon fill states" does this. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/commits/main
research.adaptive_layout:
Official breakpoints
[F] https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/breakpoints/overview. M3 now calls these "breakpoints" (formerly window size classes) and states that they "apply to Android and web."

| Breakpoint | Width | Panes | Navigation | Margins and spacer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compact | <600dp | 1 | Navigation bar or modal expanded rail; dialogs may be full-screen; supplemental selection uses a bottom sheet | 16dp |
| Medium | 600–839dp | 1 recommended, 2 only for low-density content (each 50%) | Rail for single-pane, nav bar for two-pane; menus instead of bottom sheets | 24dp |
| Expanded | 840–1199dp | 1 or 2 (2 recommended) | Collapsed or expanded rail | 24dp; a fixed pane in fixed-plus-flexible layouts is 360dp |
| Large | 1200–1599dp | 2 recommended | Rail | 24dp; fixed pane 412dp |
| Extra-large | ≥1600dp | 1 to 3 | Expanded rail suits it best | 24dp; a third pane may be a standard side sheet (max 400dp); never more than 3 panes |

Sources [F]: https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/breakpoints/compact, /medium, /expanded and /large-extra-large.
[F] Swap components across breakpoints: nav bar becomes a collapsed rail, the collapsed rail becomes an expanded rail, a bottom sheet becomes a menu. Keep text at 40–60 characters per line. Layouts must change dynamically on rotation, fold or unfold, split-screen and window resize. (overview URL above)
[F] Height classes exist on Android: compact <480dp (99.78% of phones in landscape), medium 480–899dp, expanded ≥900dp. Android also calls large and extra-large "extensions" for desktop. https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/layouts/adaptive/use-window-size-classes
[F] On medium screens the top 25% is hard to reach, so limit interactions there. https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/breakpoints/medium

Canonical layouts [F]
- List-detail, supporting pane and feed: https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/canonical-examples/overview
- Supporting pane: below the focus pane, flexible width, on compact and medium (a bottom sheet works on compact); beside it, fixed 360dp, on expanded. https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/canonical-examples/supporting-pane

Sheet rules [F]
- Bottom sheets span the full width up to 640dp. Above a 640dp window they get 56dp side and top margins; the top margin is 72dp otherwise. https://m3.material.io/components/bottom-sheets/specs
- Standard side sheets suit medium and expanded screens; modal side sheets are preferred on compact. They usually sit on the right, can be inset 16dp, scroll independently, never scroll horizontally, and mirror in RTL. https://m3.material.io/components/side-sheets/guidelines
- Docked side-sheet token width is 256px. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/latest/sass/_md-comp-sheet-side.scss

Navigation sizes [F] (from tokens)
- Collapsed rail 96px (narrow 80px); expanded rail 220–360px; nav bar 64px; floating toolbar 64px.
- https://github.com/material-components/material-web/tree/main/tokens/versions/latest/sass

Touch targets [F]
- At least 48×48dp, separated by 8dp or more. https://support.google.com/accessibility/android/answer/7101858

Recommendations for the map viewer (embeddable) [I]
1. Measure the widget, not the window. The viewer lives inside a third-party <div>, so derive the breakpoint from the host element's own width using a ResizeObserver plus CSS container queries (container-type: size on :host, then @container rules at 600/840/1200/1600px).
   - Container queries have been Baseline widely available since 2025-08. https://webstatus.dev/features/container-queries
   - Also feed a height class (<480px means compact height) into the layout.
2. Call map.resize() from that ResizeObserver.
   - [F] Mapbox GL JS 3.32.0 only listens to the window "resize" event; I found no ResizeObserver in the bundle. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mapbox-gl@3.32.0/dist/mapbox-gl.js
   - [F] trackResize is window-based. https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/api/map/
   - [I] So a host-driven container resize would otherwise leave a stretched canvas.
3. Compact (<600)
   - Full-bleed map with 16dp insets for floating controls.
   - Timeline: a floating horizontal toolbar or a peeking bottom sheet near the bottom (year chips or slider plus play button), at least 48dp tall.
   - Layers, opacity and compare: a modal bottom sheet.
   - Photo detail: an expanded bottom sheet (draggable to full screen) or a full-screen dialog.
   - About/credits: a full-screen dialog.
   - Other actions: a FAB menu (layers, compare, locate, about). A nav bar is usually unnecessary because the viewer has one destination.
4. Compact height (landscape phones, <480 high)
   - Put the timeline in a vertical floating toolbar on the trailing edge.
   - Use modal side sheets instead of bottom sheets so the map stays visible.
5. Medium (600–839)
   - Single-pane map.
   - Timeline as a floating toolbar, bottom center.
   - Layers in a modal side sheet, or a bottom sheet capped at 640dp.
   - Photo detail as a modal side sheet. 24dp margins.
6. Expanded (840–1199)
   - Map plus a standard side sheet as the supporting pane, fixed 360dp, for photo detail or the layer list; the map shrinks rather than being covered.
   - Timeline docked at the bottom of the map pane. Menus replace bottom sheets.
7. Large (1200–1599)
   - Supporting pane 412dp.
   - Optional collapsed rail, if the embed has sections such as Map, Photos and About.
8. Extra-large (≥1600, including 4K and ultrawide)
   - Up to three regions: an expanded rail or layer panel (≤360), the map, and a photo-detail side sheet (≤400).
   - Cap text line length at 40–60 characters.
   - Do not upscale controls; let the map take the space.
   - Size type in rem so user zoom works. On HiDPI or 4K screens rely on devicePixelRatio. Mapbox renders at DPR by default (behavior not re-verified here).
9. Foldables and resizable windows
   - Treat folding or unfolding as an ordinary breakpoint change, as M3 prescribes.
   - Keep state (selected photo, year) when panes are restructured.
10. Viewport units and safe areas
   - In full-screen mode use 100dvh or 100svh rather than 100vh (Baseline widely available since 2025-06; https://webstatus.dev/features/viewport-unit-variants).
   - Pad floating controls with env(safe-area-inset-*) (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/env). These insets are non-zero only if the host page sets viewport-fit=cover, which the embed cannot control, so fall back to 16dp.
11. Input and motion
   - Use @media (pointer: coarse) to enforce 48dp targets and show drag handles; with a fine pointer show hover states and tooltips.
   - Map gestures: consider cooperativeGestures: true for inline (not full-screen) embeds so page scrolling is not hijacked. https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/api/map/
   - Honor prefers-reduced-motion by switching to the standard scheme or no motion.

Recommendations for the admin SPA [I]
- List-detail for the data tables plus an editor; supporting pane for map-based placement (map plus a 360/412dp form pane).
- Wizard: a stepper in a single pane on compact and medium; a step list in the leading pane on expanded.
- Navigation: nav bar on compact, collapsed rail on medium and expanded, expanded rail on large and extra-large. Do not use a navigation drawer; it is deprecated in Expressive.
- Data tables: card or list layout on compact; horizontally scrollable table with a sticky first column on medium; full table on expanded and up.
research.recommendation:
Recommendation in brief [I]
- Use Lit for both apps rather than Preact, and treat "latest Material Design" as M3 plus the Expressive update.
- Build the M3 Expressive layer ourselves from Google's official tokens and color utilities.
- Borrow components from M3E (and, selectively, MWC Labs CSS) instead of adopting any single library wholesale.

1. Why Lit rather than Preact
- [F] Every viable M3 web-component library is built on Lit: @material/web, the MWC Labs code, @m3e/web (peer dependency lit ^3.3.0), mdui (lit ^3.3.0) and material-esm. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@m3e/web@2.10.0/package.json and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mdui@2.1.5/package.json
- [I] With Lit there is no second runtime, and native custom elements plus Shadow DOM give the style isolation the CDN embed needs.
- [M] Size check: lit-html core is 3.4 KB gzip; Preact 11.0.1 is 4.8 KB gzip plus 1.5 KB for hooks.
- [F] Preact 11.0.1 was published 2026-10-08 (https://www.npmjs.com/package/preact).
- [I] I found no maintained M3 component library for Preact. Choosing Preact means hand-building every component, or shipping Lit anyway for Lit-based components.
- [I] Preact is still workable if the team strongly prefers JSX: render into an attachShadow root (or use preact-custom-element 4.6.0) and use MWC Labs CSS classes plus your own tokens.

2. Embeddable viewer (CDN bundle, must not leak CSS)
- Ship one custom element, for example <bd-map-viewer>, with an open shadow root.
- Adopt these stylesheets into the shadow root: mapbox-gl.css, a build-time-generated token sheet scoped to :host, and the component CSS.
- Only allowed global side effect: one document-level @font-face sheet for Google Sans Flex or Roboto Flex. [F] @font-face does not work inside shadow roots. https://robdodson.me/posts/at-font-face-doesnt-work-in-shadow-dom/
- Components (about 10): floating toolbar (timeline), loading indicator, FAB menu, button group or segmented control (compare modes), icon buttons, slider (opacity and swipe), bottom sheet and side sheet, dialog (about), snackbar, chips.
- Two ways to get them:
  a) Fastest: per-component imports from @m3e/web 2.10.0 (nav-rail 2 KB, bottom-sheet 5.8 KB, slider 7.3 KB, button 7.8 KB, plus core 23.6 KB, all gzip [M]). Skip <m3e-theme> (26.7 KB [M]) and pre-generate the --md-sys-* tokens instead.
  b) Leanest and most "Google-exact": hand-build the components in Lit. Values come from @material/web@2.5.0 tokens/versions/latest; pin the exact version, because [F] it may break in minor releases (https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/README.md). Vendor the MWC Labs gb CSS for buttons, icon buttons, FAB, split button, menu, list, switch and card (Apache-2.0, already in @layer), rewriting :root to :host.
- [I] Target budget: under about 40 KB gzip of UI on top of Mapbox.

3. Admin SPA (not embedded; style leakage matters less)
- Lit plus @m3e/web: datepicker, timepicker, stepper (wizard), paginator, select, autocomplete, form field, nav rail and bar, toolbar, split pane, bottom sheet, snackbar, tabs, progress and loading indicator.
- Optionally use the stable @material/web 2.5.0 form controls (text field, select, checkbox, radio, switch, slider, dialog, menu, chips). [I] Both libraries read --md-sys-* tokens, so one generated theme drives both.
- Data tables: [F] no M3 web library ships a real data-table component. [I] Use a headless table library rendered with M3 tokens (surface-container rows, outline-variant dividers, label-lg headers).
- File upload: [I] a custom drop zone made from an M3 card plus progress indicator.

4. Expressive look, regardless of library
- Color: MCU 0.4.0 with specVersion '2025' and variant TONAL_SPOT (or VIBRANT / EXPRESSIVE for a bolder look), seeded from a brand color. Ship light, dark, medium-contrast and high-contrast schemes.
- Shape: the full corner scale including 20, 32 and 48px, pill-shaped primary actions, and the 35-shape library for photo-thumbnail crops. Morph with clip-path: polygon(), or with CSS shape() as progressive enhancement.
- Motion: --md-sys-motion-spring-* variables set to Google's official web cubic-bezier conversions, or linear() curves generated from the official stiffness and damping (for example fast spatial 1400 / 0.9). Use JS springs only for drag gestures on sheets. Honor reduced motion.
- Type: emphasized styles, using the ROND axis on Google Sans Flex.
- Navigation: never a drawer; use the collapsed or expanded rail.
- Pick one or two "hero moments," for example the timeline year scrubber and the photo reveal.

5. Risks to watch [I]
- M3E has a single maintainer, so pin versions and keep a thin wrapper layer so components can be swapped.
- MWC Labs is Google's likely future official implementation. Re-evaluate when Labs components graduate or m3.material.io/develop/web stops saying "Expressive is not implemented on Web."
- Avoid MUI (Material Design 2). Avoid mdui v2 for the "latest" requirement: it is M3 baseline and its Expressive v3 looks stalled.
- Avoid Beer CSS for the embed: the default build styles global elements and it has no Shadow DOM. It is acceptable for the admin if you prefer a CSS-only approach.

verification:
I re-checked the research on 2026-10-11 against npm, GitHub, jsDelivr, webstatus.dev and m3.material.io (rendered in a browser). Almost all of it holds. I found two factual errors, two significant omissions and a few minor inaccuracies. The recommendation still holds, with the adjustments listed in section E. The two mdui caveats:
- The v3 branch's last commit is dated 2025-08-13 by author date but 2025-08-15 by commit date. Either way, v3 appears stalled.

Other claims confirmed:

  - mdui: 83,547 for the JS and 3,476 for the CSS
  - Beer CSS: 16,878 for the CSS and 5,864 for the JS; material-dynamic-colors: 16,345

- **Token values:** design-system version 34.0.21, all six spring stiffness/damping pairs, the shape scale (20/32/48px), nav rail collapsed 96px (narrow 80px), expanded rail 220–360px, nav bar 64px, floating toolbar 64px, docked side sheet 256px, bottom-sheet drag handle 32×4. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/tree/main/tokens/versions/latest/sass
- **Color utilities 0.4.0:** SpecVersion is '2021' | '2025', the nine variants match, contrast runs from -1 to 1, and the constructor signature is correct.
- **MWC theming docs:** they do say MWC does not support --md-ref-palette or --md-sys-motion. https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/docs/theming/README.md
- **M3E:** has 35 shapes, the dependencies and peer dependencies are as stated, and the README disclaims any Google affiliation.
- **Beer CSS:** the README claims "Latest M3 Expressive already"; the `<beer-css>` element has no attachShadow; 5.0.3 added the module build.
- **Mapbox GL JS 3.32.0:** no ResizeObserver in the bundle. It listens only to window resize, orientationchange and fullscreenchange (mapbox-gl-dev.js lines 107795–107797).
- **Google Sans Flex:** the CSS2 API URL returns HTTP 200 and Fontsource lists it as OFL-1.1.

## B. Corrections and omissions

1. **[Error] linear() Baseline date is wrong.** The research says "Baseline widely available since 2023-12." It became newly available on 2023-12-11 and widely available only on 2026-06-11. https://api.webstatus.dev/v1/features/linear-easing — The conclusion that it is safe to use still holds.

2. **[Omission] Google's color utilities have a newer, unreleased spec.** The upstream source already has `SpecVersion = '2021'|'2025'|'2026'`, with color_spec_2026.ts added 2026-02-17 ("Added CMF Scheme in 2026 spec"). It also has a 2026-07-27 fix, "Updated PrimaryContainer color calculation for Expressive dark mode." Neither is in the npm 0.4.0 release. https://github.com/material-foundation/material-color-utilities/blob/main/typescript/dynamiccolor/color_spec.ts
   - [I] Generating colors with npm 0.4.0 and spec '2025' gives slightly older Expressive dark-mode primary containers.
   - [I] Build the generator from the GitHub source pinned to a commit, or accept the small differences. This is likely why m3-svelte depends on a nightly build.

3. **[Omission] MICL is a framework-agnostic Expressive library the research missed.** MICL (`material-inspired-component-library`):
   - [F] Version 10.0.0, published 2026-09-27; MIT; 22 stars; one maintainer (henkpb, 566 commits).
   - [F] Built from native HTML plus CSS classes, with no custom elements and no runtime dependencies. The README claims about 14 kB gzip of JavaScript for the whole library.
   - [F] 30 component folders, including bottom sheet, side sheet, navigation rail, navigation bar, button group, split button, date picker, time picker and stepper. https://github.com/henkpb/micl
   - It was also mentioned in MWC discussion #5642.
   - [F] A second missed library is @vollowx/seele 0.14.3 (published 2026-09-26, Lit-based, 21 stars, one maintainer).
   - This weakens two of the research's claims: "every viable M3 library is built on Lit" and "no maintained M3 library for Preact." MICL is markup-plus-classes, so it fits Preact. It is very small and its Expressive claims are self-reported, but it belongs in the comparison.

4. **[Error, misleading comparison] The Lit vs Preact size comparison measures the wrong thing.** The research compares lit-html alone (3.2 KB) against Preact plus hooks (6.5 KB). Building custom elements needs the full Lit runtime: lit-html 3,222 + @lit/reactive-element 2,381 + lit-element 576 ≈ 6.2 KB gzip. Preact 11.0.1 is 4,960, plus 1,582 for hooks, ≈ 6.5 KB.
   - [I] The two are effectively the same size. Size does not favor Lit.
   - [I] M3E's per-component sizes also exclude Lit and tslib, which are peer dependencies imported separately (checked in the import lines of button.min.js).

## C. Minor inaccuracies

1. **"Deprecated" vs "no longer recommended."** The research calls the navigation drawer "deprecated in Expressive." Google's wording is "no longer recommended in the Material 3 Expressive update," and the drawer is listed as "Unavailable" on web. https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-drawer/overview
2. **Android does not call large and extra-large "extensions."** The Android docs say they "have been added to better target desktop and connected displays." They are opt-in through `supportLargeAndXLargeWidth = true`. The height-class values (480 and 900dp, and 99.78% of phones in landscape) are correct. https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/layouts/adaptive/use-window-size-classes
3. **sober's repo has moved and has an active 2.0 line.** The repo is now miralm-ltd/sober (242 stars, pushed 2026-09-25). It also has a 2.0.0-alpha.20 release from 2026-09-22 that the research did not mention.
4. **MWC Labs on main has more than listed.** Main also includes appbar and chip classes, both added 2026-07-21. Main's labs/gb/components now has 22 components.
5. **Google Sans Flex is not an M3 recommendation.** The M3 fonts page names Roboto (the default), Roboto Flex ("aren't yet part of the M3 typescale") and Noto Sans, and does not mention Google Sans Flex. https://m3.material.io/styles/typography/fonts — Using Google Sans Flex first is a reasonable inference, not an M3 rule.
6. **light-dark() is not yet widely available.** It has been newly available since 2024-05-13, so it needs a fallback, as the research says.
7. **Other Baseline dates are correct:** container queries widely available 2025-08-14, viewport units 2025-06-05, and shape() newly available 2026-02-24 (webstatus.dev).

## D. Material Design pages (m3.material.io) — all confirmed

- **Breakpoints, confirmed verbatim:**
  - Compact: under 600dp
  - Medium: 600–839dp
  - Expanded: 840–1199dp
  - Large: 1200–1599dp
  - Extra-large: 1600dp+
  - The page says the term was "previously window size class" and that breakpoints "apply to Android and web." Height breakpoints are Android-only.
  - Margins are 16dp on compact and 24dp on all others.
  - Fixed pane is 360dp on expanded and 412dp on large and extra-large.
  - On extra-large, a third pane can be a side sheet with a maximum width of 400dp; never more than three panes.
  - On medium, use a rail for single-pane layouts and a nav bar for two-pane layouts, with each pane at 50%.
  - On medium, avoid placing interactions in the top 25% of the screen.
  - Pages: https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/breakpoints/overview, /compact, /medium, /expanded and /large-extra-large
- **Expressive on the web:** the /develop/web page says verbatim: "Material Web Components are currently in maintenance mode. No updates are currently being made to this library. Material 3 Expressive is not implemented on Web." It adds, about Angular Material: "Implementation may differ from Material Web Components and these guidelines."
- **Shape morph:** "Web is not currently available."
- **Motion:** web is listed as "Compatible," and all 12 spring-to-curve values match the research.
- **Baseline navigation rail:** "no longer recommended," replaced by the collapsed rail.
- **Bottom sheets:** full width up to 640dp; above 640dp, 56dp top and side margins; otherwise a 72dp top margin.
- **Expressive announcement:** published May 13, 2025; "not M4" and M3 is not deprecated; 46 studies with more than 18,000 participants; 14 components; 35 shapes; "one or two" hero moments.

## E. Does the recommendation still hold?

Mostly yes. Every central fact behind it checks out:
- Expressive is officially not implemented on the web.
- MWC is in maintenance mode, while Google is building Expressive components in MWC Labs.
- M3E is the broadest Lit-based Expressive library but has a single maintainer.
- The token, breakpoint and motion values are all correct.
- MUI is still Material Design 2, and mdui v2 is non-Expressive with v3 stalled.

The amendments [I]:
1. **Lit vs Preact.** Base the choice on ecosystem fit, not size. The runtimes are about 6.2 KB vs 6.5 KB gzip. If the team prefers JSX, Preact plus a CSS-first layer (MWC Labs gb CSS, or MICL) is a real option. Lit is still the better fit if you want to use M3E or MWC components.
2. **Add MICL to the comparison.** List it as a framework-agnostic, CSS-first Expressive option, with a bus-factor-1 warning similar to M3E's.
3. **Color generation.** Generate the theme from the color-utilities GitHub source pinned to a commit (it has the 2026 spec and the Expressive dark-mode fix), or note that npm 0.4.0 is behind.
4. **Wording.** Fix the linear() date and say "no longer recommended" instead of "deprecated" for the drawer.
5. **Bundle budget.** Count Lit (about 6.2 KB) and tslib separately when estimating the M3E-based embed size.
